edition.locus: Documenta Catholica Omnia Canones GR (sources/canones_GR.pdf), p. 2, Canon ε´

source_text: Ἄλλοι δὲ ἑαυτοὺς ἐξαπατῶσιν, ἀντὶ τῶν ἰδίων τῶν ἀπωλομένων, ἃ εὗρον ἀλλότρια κατέχοντες, ἵνα, ἐπειδὴ αὐτοὺς Βοράδοι καὶ Γότθοι τὰ τῶν πολεμίων εἰργάσαντο, αὐτοὶ ἄλλοις Βοράδοι καὶ Γότθοι γίνωνται. Ἀπεστείλαμεν οὖν τὸν ἀδελφὸν καὶ συγγέροντα Εὐφρόσυνον διὰ ταῦτα πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἵνα κατὰ τὸν ἐνθάδε τύπον καὶ αὐτὸς δῴῃ ὁμοίως, καὶ ὧν δεῖ τὰς κατηγορίας προσίεσθαι, καὶ οὓς δεῖ ἐκκηρῦξαι τῶν εὐχῶν.
thought_title: Robbing others to make up for one’s own losses
orientation: Gregory rebukes those who make up their own losses by keeping goods that belong to others, and sends Euphrosynus to apply the same discipline that Gregory's own church keeps.
pass_a_gloss: Others deceive themselves, holding the others' things which they found, in place of their own lost things, so that, since Boradi and Goths worked on them the things of enemies, they themselves become Boradi and Goths to others. We sent therefore the brother and fellow-elder Euphrosynus on account of these things to you, so that according to the pattern here he too may give likewise, both [as to] whose accusations one must admit, and whom one must proclaim out from the prayers.

choices.why: Keeps both possible senses open: a fellow presbyter, or a companion in old age.

The print's reading is followed; δῴῃ has no expressed object, and the two clauses that follow are what he is to give direction about. Vossius' Latin suggests a Greek with 'there' (ἐκεῖ); no Greek witness was in hand to check it.

choices.english: have dealt with them as enemies
choices.why: Idiom for doing to someone what enemies do.

pass_b_english: Others deceive themselves by keeping other people’s goods that they have found in place of their own that were lost, so that, because the Boradi and the Goths have dealt with them as enemies, they themselves become Boradi and Goths to others. For this reason, then, we have sent our brother and fellow elder Euphrosynus to you, so that he too may give direction in the same way, following the practice we keep here, as to whose accusations ought to be accepted and who ought to be shut out of the prayers.
notes: Rubric left out (editorial). Βοράδοι καὶ Γότθοι = the Boradi and the Goths, the raiders of Pontus. τὰ τῶν πολεμίων εἰργάσαντο rendered 'have dealt with them as enemies'. συγγέρων rendered 'fellow elder' (fellow presbyter). δῴῃ has no expressed object; 'direction' is supplied for English, and the two clauses that follow are what he is to give direction about. Doubtful reading: Vossius' Latin ('ut secundum formam quae hic est, etiam ibi det similiter') suggests his Greek had 'there' (ἐκεῖ) where this print has αὐτός ('he too'); the English follows the print. ἐκκηρῦξαι τῶν εὐχῶν rendered 'shut out of the prayers'. No Scripture.
